role.en: Sapa Inca, founder of the Inca Empire
role.zh: 萨帕印卡，印加帝国奠基者

summary.en: A younger son of Viracocha Inca, Cusi Yupanqui saved Cusco from the Chanka and took the name Pachacuti, “world-turner”. He rebuilt the capital, reorganised Inca religion and began the conquests that made Tawantinsuyu an empire; Machu Picchu was one of his royal estates.
summary.zh: 库西·尤潘基是维拉科查·印卡的幼子，他从昌卡人手中拯救了库斯科，取名帕查库蒂，意为“扭转乾坤者”。他重建首都、改组印加宗教，并开启了使塔万廷苏尤成为帝国的征服；马丘比丘是他的王室庄园之一。

label.zh: 在亚瓦尔潘帕击败昌卡人
加冕为萨帕印卡，重建库斯科

label.en: Builds the royal estate of Machu Picchu
label.zh: 修建马丘比丘王室庄园

label.en: Conquers the Colla at Hatuncolla, Lake Titicaca
label.zh: 在的的喀喀湖畔哈通科利亚征服科利亚人

label.en: Dies in Cusco after handing power to Topa Inca
label.zh: 传位图帕克·印卡后卒于库斯科

story.en:
According to the chronicler Juan de Betanzos, who married an Inca princess, the Chanka confederation marched on Cusco when Viracocha Inca was old. The king and his heir Urco fled, but the young prince Cusi Yupanqui stayed to defend the city. Inca tradition said that the stones of the fields rose up as warriors, the pururauca, to fight beside him.

After the victory he took the name Pachacuti and the royal fringe. He is credited with rebuilding Cusco in stone, raising the Coricancha to the Sun and ordering the histories of the dynasty, so much of what the Spanish later heard about earlier kings passed through his reforms.

His armies conquered the Lake Titicaca basin and much of the central Andes, and his son Topa Inca carried the conquests further. A legal document of 1568 found in Cusco archives in the 1980s shows that Machu Picchu belonged to Pachacuti’s descendants.
story.zh:
据娶了印加公主的编年史家胡安·德·贝坦索斯记载，维拉科查·印卡年老时，昌卡联盟进军库斯科。国王和继承人乌尔科出逃，年轻的王子库西·尤潘基却留下守城。印加传说称，田野里的石头化为战士“普鲁劳卡”，与他并肩作战。

获胜后他取名帕查库蒂，戴上了王者的流苏冠饰。人们认为是他用石材重建库斯科、为太阳神扩建科里坎查神殿，并整理王朝历史，因此西班牙人后来听到的有关早期君主的说法，大多经过了他的改造。

他的军队征服了的的喀喀湖盆地和中部安第斯的大片地区，其子图帕克·印卡进一步扩张。20世纪80年代在库斯科档案中发现的一份1568年法律文书表明，马丘比丘属于帕查库蒂的后裔。

sources.title: Britannica: Pachacuti Inca Yupanqui
Juan de Betanzos, Suma y narración de los Incas (1551)
John H. Rowe, “Machu Picchu a la luz de documentos de siglo XVI”, Histórica 14 (1990)

note: His birth year is unknown: 1418 is a common estimate and some works give c. 1391. The reign of 1438–1471 follows Rowe’s conventional chronology; the Yahuarpampa victory is known only from Inca oral tradition.

role.zh: 萨帕印卡、征服者

summary.en: Pachacuti’s son and general extended the empire north to Quito, along the coast through the Chimú kingdom and south into Chile, roughly tripling its size. Chroniclers credit him with organising provincial administration and the decimal census.
summary.zh: 帕查库蒂之子兼大将，将帝国向北扩张至基多，沿海征服奇穆王国，向南深入智利，疆域约扩大三倍。编年史家认为他建立了行省管理和十进制户籍制度。

label.en: Campaigns in the north as far as Quito
Conquers Chimor and takes its king to Cusco
label.zh: 征服奇莫尔，将其国王带回库斯科

label.en: Sets the southern frontier near the Maule river
label.zh: 将南部边界推进至马乌莱河附近

label.en: Dies at his estate of Chinchero

sources.title: Britannica: Topa Inca Yupanqui
Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa, Historia de los Incas (1572)
Terence N. D’Altroy, The Incas (2nd ed., 2015)

note: Dates follow Rowe’s chronology and are approximate.

role.zh: 萨帕印卡

summary.en: The last Sapa Inca to rule an undivided empire spent much of his reign campaigning in the north, where he made Tumebamba a second capital. He died around 1527, probably of smallpox that had spread ahead of the Spanish, leaving the succession open between Huáscar and Atahualpa.
summary.zh: 最后一位统治统一帝国的萨帕印卡，在位期间多在北方征战，将图米班巴建为第二首都。约1527年去世，很可能死于先于西班牙人传入的天花，留下瓦斯卡尔与阿塔瓦尔帕之间的继承之争。

label.en: Builds Tumebamba as a northern capital
label.zh: 将图米班巴建为北方首都
在亚瓦尔科查镇压卡兰基人

label.en: Dies of an epidemic in Quito

sources.title: Britannica: Huayna Capac
Pedro Cieza de León, El señorío de los Incas (c. 1553)
Terence N. D’Altroy, The Incas (2nd ed., 2015)

note: Birth year and place vary in the sources; death is dated 1525–1528.

role.en: Last Sapa Inca of the empire
role.zh: 印加帝国末代萨帕印卡

summary.en: A son of Huayna Capac based in the north, Atahualpa won the civil war against his half-brother Huáscar in 1532, only to be captured by Francisco Pizarro at Cajamarca days later. He paid a ransom of a room filled with gold and silver but was executed in July 1533.
summary.zh: 瓦伊纳·卡帕克之子，驻守北方。1532年他在内战中战胜同父异母兄弟瓦斯卡尔，几天后却在卡哈马卡被弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗俘虏。他交付了装满一屋的金银作为赎金，仍于1533年7月被处决。

label.en: Born, probably in Quito or Cusco
label.zh: 出生，可能在基多或库斯科

label.en: Commands the northern armies at Quito
His generals defeat Huáscar at Quipaipan
label.zh: 其将领在基派潘击败瓦斯卡尔
在卡哈马卡被皮萨罗俘虏

story.en:
In November 1532 Atahualpa was resting at the hot springs outside Cajamarca with a victorious army, while his generals marched his captive brother Huáscar towards him. He agreed to meet the 168 Spaniards in the town square, carried on a litter and attended by thousands of unarmed retainers.

The friar Vicente de Valverde handed him a breviary and demanded that he submit to Christianity and the Spanish king. Accounts say Atahualpa looked at the book and let it fall; the hidden Spaniards opened fire with guns and cavalry and seized him in the panic.

In captivity he learned chess and offered to fill a room once with gold and twice with silver. The treasure was melted into some six tonnes of gold, but in July 1533 Pizarro’s men accused him of plotting an attack and executed him by garrotte after he accepted baptism to avoid burning.
story.zh:
1532年11月，阿塔瓦尔帕率得胜之师在卡哈马卡城外温泉休憩，他的将领正押着被俘的兄长瓦斯卡尔前来。他同意在城中广场会见168名西班牙人，乘坐轿舆，由数千名未携武器的侍从簇拥而至。

修士比森特·德·巴尔韦德递给他一本祈祷书，要求他皈依基督教、臣服西班牙国王。据记载，阿塔瓦尔帕看了看书便任其落地；埋伏的西班牙人随即开枪、骑兵冲杀，在混乱中将他擒获。

被囚期间他学会了下国际象棋，并提出用黄金填满一间屋子一次、用白银填满两次作为赎金。这批财宝熔铸出约六吨黄金，但1533年7月皮萨罗的部下指控他密谋袭击，他为免火刑接受洗礼后被绞死。

sources.title: Britannica: Atahuallpa
Francisco de Xerez, Verdadera relación de la conquista del Perú (1534)
John Hemming, The Conquest of the Incas (1970)

note: Birth year (c. 1500–1502) and birthplace are disputed.

role.en: Sapa Inca, leader of the Inca resistance
role.zh: 萨帕印卡，印加抵抗运动领袖

summary.en: Installed as a puppet ruler by Pizarro in 1533, Manco rebelled in 1536, besieging Cusco for ten months with a huge army. After defeating the Spanish at Ollantaytambo he withdrew to Vilcabamba and founded the Neo-Inca State; he was murdered by Spanish refugees he had sheltered.
summary.zh: 1533年被皮萨罗立为傀儡君主，1536年起兵反抗，率大军围攻库斯科达十个月。他在奥扬泰坦博击败西班牙人后退入比尔卡班巴，建立新印加国，后被他收留的西班牙逃亡者杀害。

label.en: Born in Cusco, son of Huayna Capac
label.zh: 生于库斯科，瓦伊纳·卡帕克之子

label.en: Crowned Sapa Inca under Spanish tutelage
label.zh: 在西班牙人扶持下加冕为萨帕印卡
从萨克塞华曼围攻库斯科
在奥扬泰坦博击退埃尔南多·皮萨罗

label.en: Establishes his court at Vitcos and Vilcabamba
label.zh: 在比特科斯与比尔卡班巴建立宫廷

sources.title: Britannica: Manco Inca
Titu Cusi Yupanqui, Instrucción (1570)
Kim MacQuarrie, The Last Days of the Incas (Simon & Schuster, 2007)

role.zh: 比尔卡班巴末代萨帕印卡

summary.en: A son of Manco Inca raised in the sacred house of Vilcabamba, Túpac Amaru became Sapa Inca in 1571. Viceroy Francisco de Toledo sent an army that took Vilcabamba in 1572; Túpac Amaru was captured in the forest and beheaded in Cusco’s main square before a grieving crowd.
summary.zh: 曼科·印卡之子，在比尔卡班巴的圣所中长大，1571年成为萨帕印卡。总督弗朗西斯科·德·托莱多派兵于1572年攻占比尔卡班巴；图帕克·阿马鲁在森林中被俘，在库斯科中央广场当着悲痛的人群被斩首。

label.zh: 在比尔卡班巴成为萨帕印卡
在库斯科中央广场被斩首

sources.title: Britannica: History of Peru
Baltasar de Ocampo, Descripción de la provincia de Vilcabamba (1610)
John Hemming, The Conquest of the Incas (1970)

role.zh: 秘鲁征服者

summary.en: An illegitimate son of a soldier from Trujillo in Extremadura, Pizarro led the small expedition that captured Atahualpa in 1532 and seized the Inca Empire. He founded Lima in 1535 and was assassinated there in 1541 by supporters of his former partner Diego de Almagro.
summary.zh: 出身埃斯特雷马杜拉特鲁希略一名军人的私生子，率领一支小型远征队于1532年俘虏阿塔瓦尔帕，夺取了印加帝国。1535年建立利马，1541年在利马被昔日合伙人迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗的支持者刺杀。

label.zh: 生于埃斯特雷马杜拉的特鲁希略

label.en: With Balboa at Darién when the Pacific is sighted
label.zh: 随巴尔沃亚在达连望见太平洋

label.en: Signs the Capitulation of Toledo with the crown
label.zh: 与王室签订《托莱多协定》
在卡哈马卡俘虏阿塔瓦尔帕

label.en: Assassinated in his palace in Lima

sources.title: Britannica: Francisco Pizarro
Francisco de Xerez, Verdadera relación de la conquista del Perú (1534)
James Lockhart, The Men of Cajamarca (University of Texas Press, 1972)

name.zh: 佩德罗·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔

role.zh: 航海家，欧洲人中巴西的发现者

summary.en: A nobleman chosen to lead Portugal’s second fleet to India, Cabral swung far west across the Atlantic and on 22 April 1500 sighted Brazil, which he claimed for King Manuel I. He continued to Calicut, losing four ships at the Cape of Good Hope, and was never given another command.
summary.zh: 受命率领葡萄牙第二支印度船队的贵族。他在大西洋中向西远航，于1500年4月22日望见巴西，为曼努埃尔一世宣称主权。随后继续驶往卡利卡特，在好望角损失四艘船，此后再未获指挥权。

label.zh: 在巴西塞古罗港附近登陆

sources.title: Britannica: Pedro Álvares Cabral
Pero Vaz de Caminha, Carta a el-Rei D. Manuel (1 May 1500)
William Brooks Greenlee (ed.), The Voyage of Pedro Álvares Cabral to Brazil and India (Hakluyt Society, 1938)

name.zh: 弗朗西斯科·德·奥雷亚纳

role.en: Conquistador; first European to descend the Amazon
role.zh: 征服者，首位沿亚马孙河而下的欧洲人

summary.en: A kinsman of the Pizarros, Orellana joined Gonzalo Pizarro’s search for the “Land of Cinnamon” east of Quito, went downriver for food in 1541 and, unable to return, sailed the whole length of the Amazon to the Atlantic in 1542. He died trying to colonise the river four years later.
summary.zh: 皮萨罗家族的亲戚，参加贡萨洛·皮萨罗在基多以东寻找“肉桂之乡”的远征。1541年他顺流而下寻找食物，因无法逆流返回，于1542年航行亚马孙河全程抵达大西洋。四年后他在试图殖民该河时去世。

label.zh: 生于埃斯特雷马杜拉的特鲁希略
随贡萨洛·皮萨罗离开基多

label.en: Reaches the mouth of the Amazon
Wins a royal licence at Valladolid
label.zh: 在巴利亚多利德获王室特许

sources.title: Britannica: Francisco de Orellana
Gaspar de Carvajal, Relación del nuevo descubrimiento del famoso río Grande (1542)
José Toribio Medina (ed.), The Discovery of the Amazon (American Geographical Society, 1934)

role.zh: 征服者，智利首任总督

summary.en: A veteran of Italy and of Pizarro’s wars, Valdivia marched south from Cusco in 1540, founded Santiago in 1541 and Concepción in 1550, and pushed into Mapuche lands. Lautaro’s warriors captured and killed him at Tucapel in December 1553.
summary.zh: 参加过意大利战争和皮萨罗征战的老兵，1540年从库斯科南下，1541年建立圣地亚哥，1550年建立康塞普西翁，并深入马普切人的土地。1553年12月他在图卡佩尔被劳塔罗的战士俘杀。

label.en: Born near Villanueva de la Serena
label.zh: 生于比利亚努埃瓦-德拉塞雷纳附近

label.en: Fights for Pizarro at Las Salinas
label.zh: 为皮萨罗参加拉斯萨利纳斯之战
在彭科建立康塞普西翁

label.en: Killed after the battle of Tucapel

sources.title: Britannica: Pedro de Valdivia
Pedro de Valdivia, Cartas de relación (1545–1552)
Jerónimo de Vivar, Crónica y relación copiosa y verdadera de los reinos de Chile (1558)

role.zh: 马普切军事首领（托基）

summary.en: Captured as a boy and made a groom in Valdivia’s household, Lautaro learned Spanish cavalry tactics, escaped and led the Mapuche to victory at Tucapel in 1553. He defeated the Spanish again at Marihueñu and marched on Santiago before being killed in a surprise attack in 1557.
summary.zh: 少年时被俘，在瓦尔迪维亚家中做马夫，学会了西班牙骑兵战术。逃回后于1553年率马普切人在图卡佩尔获胜，又在马里韦努击败西班牙人，进军圣地亚哥，1557年在一次突袭中阵亡。

label.en: Serves as a captive groom to Valdivia in Santiago
label.zh: 在圣地亚哥为瓦尔迪维亚做被俘马夫

label.en: Defeats Francisco de Villagra at Marihueñu
label.zh: 在马里韦努击败弗朗西斯科·德·比利亚格拉

label.en: Killed at Peteroa on the Mataquito
label.zh: 在马塔基托河畔佩特罗阿阵亡

sources.title: Wikipedia: Lautaro
Alonso de Ercilla, La Araucana (1569–1589)
José Bengoa, Historia del pueblo mapuche (1985)

note: Birth year is approximate; early life known mainly from Spanish chroniclers and Ercilla’s epic.

name.zh: 印卡·加西拉索·德拉维加

role.zh: 编年史家、历史学家

summary.en: Born in Cusco to a Spanish captain and the Inca princess Chimpu Ocllo, Garcilaso left for Spain at 21 and never returned. His Comentarios Reales (1609) presented the Incas as a civilised monarchy and became the most influential account of Inca history for two centuries.
summary.zh: 生于库斯科，父亲为西班牙上尉，母亲为印加公主琴普·奥克略。21岁赴西班牙，终身未返。其《印卡王室述评》（1609年）把印加描绘为文明的君主国，两百年间是关于印加历史最有影响的著作。

label.en: Settles with his uncle at Montilla

label.zh: 《印卡王室述评》在里斯本出版

label.en: Dies in Córdoba; buried in the Mezquita
label.zh: 卒于科尔多瓦，葬于大清真寺主教座堂

story.en:
As a boy in Cusco, Gómez Suárez de Figueroa listened to his mother’s relatives recount the history of the Incas and saw the mummies of the Inca kings before they were sent to Lima. At 21 he sailed to Spain to claim his late father’s rights, failed, fought against the Morisco rebels of the Alpujarras and settled into a quiet life in Andalusia.

Taking the name Inca Garcilaso de la Vega, he first translated León Hebreo’s Dialogues of Love from Italian and wrote La Florida on Hernando de Soto’s expedition. In 1609 he published the Comentarios Reales, written from memory, letters from Cusco and Spanish chronicles, defending the Incas as wise lawgivers.

The second part, on the conquest, appeared after his death in 1617. After the Túpac Amaru rebellion of 1780 the Spanish crown banned the book in Peru as dangerous; UNESCO later honoured him as a founder of mestizo literature.
story.zh:
少年戈麦斯·苏亚雷斯·德·菲格罗亚在库斯科常听母亲的族人讲述印加历史，还在印加君主的木乃伊被运往利马之前亲眼见过它们。21岁时他远赴西班牙为亡父争取权益，未能如愿，后参加镇压阿尔普哈拉斯摩里斯科人起义，在安达卢西亚过起平静的生活。

他改名印卡·加西拉索·德拉维加，先从意大利文翻译了莱昂·埃布雷奥的《爱的对话》，又写了记述埃尔南多·德·索托远征的《佛罗里达》。1609年他凭借记忆、库斯科来信和西班牙编年史出版了《印卡王室述评》，为印加作为贤明立法者辩护。

记述征服的第二部在他死后于1617年出版。1780年图帕克·阿马鲁起义后，西班牙王室以危险为由在秘鲁查禁此书；后世则尊他为混血文学的奠基人。

sources.title: Britannica: Garcilaso de la Vega
Inca Garcilaso de la Vega, Comentarios Reales de los Incas (Lisbon, 1609)
John Grier Varner, El Inca: The Life and Times of Garcilaso de la Vega (University of Texas Press, 1968)

name.zh: 费利佩·瓦曼·波马·德·阿亚拉

role.zh: 安第斯编年史家、插画家

summary.en: An Indigenous noble from Lucanas, Guaman Poma served Spanish churchmen as an interpreter, then spent decades writing the Nueva corónica y buen gobierno, a 1,189-page letter to Philip III with nearly 400 drawings denouncing colonial abuses. It was rediscovered in Copenhagen in 1908.
summary.zh: 卢卡纳斯的原住民贵族，曾为西班牙教士担任翻译，此后用数十年写成《新编年史与善政》——一封致腓力三世、长达1189页并附近400幅插图的长信，控诉殖民暴政。1908年在哥本哈根被重新发现。

label.zh: 生于卢卡纳斯省（年份约略）

label.en: Assists Cristóbal de Albornoz’s campaign against Taki Unquy around Huamanga
label.zh: 在瓦曼加一带协助克里斯托瓦尔·德·阿尔沃诺斯打击“塔基·翁基”运动

label.en: Loses a land lawsuit and is banished from Huamanga
label.zh: 土地诉讼败诉，被逐出瓦曼加

label.en: Travels to Lima to send his chronicle to the king
label.zh: 前往利马将编年史寄呈国王

story.en:
Guaman Poma claimed descent from the Yarovilca lords of Huánuco and from Topa Inca. He knew colonial society from the inside, working for the inspector Cristóbal de Albornoz as he hunted down the Taki Unquy, a dancing movement that called on the Andean gods to drive out the Spanish.

After losing his lands in court, he wandered the Andes as an old man and poured his experience into the Nueva corónica y buen gobierno. Its ink drawings show Inca kings, the agricultural calendar, the khipu-keeper with his knotted cords, and priests and officials abusing Andean people. He urged the king to restore native lords and keep Spaniards out of Indigenous towns.

The manuscript somehow reached Denmark and lay unnoticed in the Royal Library in Copenhagen until the German scholar Richard Pietschmann identified it in 1908. Today it is one of the most important sources on Andean life, and the library has published it online.
story.zh:
瓦曼·波马自称是瓦努科亚罗维尔卡领主和图帕克·印卡的后裔。他深谙殖民社会内情，曾为巡察官克里斯托瓦尔·德·阿尔沃诺斯效力，追查“塔基·翁基”——一场呼唤安第斯神灵驱逐西班牙人的舞蹈运动。

在诉讼中失去土地后，年迈的他游历安第斯各地，把毕生见闻倾注于《新编年史与善政》。书中的墨线插图描绘了印加君主、农事历法、手持结绳的“基普”记录官，以及欺压安第斯百姓的神父和官吏。他恳请国王恢复原住民首领的权力，禁止西班牙人进入原住民村镇。

这部手稿不知如何流入丹麦，在哥本哈根皇家图书馆中沉睡，直到1908年德国学者理查德·皮奇曼才将其认出。如今它是研究安第斯生活最重要的史料之一，该图书馆已将其全文上网。

sources.title: Britannica: Felipe Guaman Poma de Ayala
Royal Danish Library, The Guaman Poma Website (GKS 2232 4°)
Rolena Adorno, Guaman Poma: Writing and Resistance in Colonial Peru (University of Texas Press, 1986)

role.en: Mystic; first canonised saint of the Americas
role.zh: 神秘主义者，美洲首位封圣者

summary.en: Isabel Flores de Oliva, a Lima girl of modest Spanish family, became a Dominican tertiary famous for severe penances and care for the sick poor. She died at 31; canonised in 1671, she is patron saint of the Americas and the Philippines.
summary.zh: 伊莎贝尔·弗洛雷斯·德·奥利瓦出身利马一个普通的西班牙家庭，成为多明我会第三会会士，以严苛苦修和照料贫病者闻名。她31岁去世，1671年封圣，是美洲和菲律宾的主保圣人。

label.en: Confirmed at Quives by Archbishop Toribio de Mogrovejo
label.zh: 在基韦斯由大主教托里维奥·德·莫格罗韦霍施坚振礼

sources.title: Britannica: Saint Rose of Lima
Ramón Mujica Pinilla, Rosa limensis: mística, política e iconografía en torno a la patrona de América (FCE, 2004)

role.zh: 帕尔马雷斯逃奴社区领袖

summary.en: Born free in Palmares, the great maroon state in the hills of Alagoas, Zumbi was taken as a baby and raised by a priest, then fled back at 15. He rejected Ganga Zumba’s 1678 peace with the governor and led the resistance until Palmares fell in 1694; he was killed on 20 November 1695.
summary.zh: 尊比生于阿拉戈斯山区的大型逃奴国家帕尔马雷斯，婴儿时被掳走由一名神父抚养，15岁逃回。他拒绝甘加·尊巴1678年与总督的和约，领导抵抗直至1694年帕尔马雷斯陷落，1695年11月20日被杀。

label.en: Raised as Francisco by a priest at Porto Calvo
label.zh: 在波尔图卡尔武由神父抚养，取名弗朗西斯科

label.en: Rejects the Cucaú treaty and takes command
label.zh: 拒绝库考条约并掌握领导权

label.en: Survives the fall of the Macaco stronghold
label.zh: 马卡科要塞陷落时突围

label.en: Betrayed and killed in the hills

story.en:
Palmares grew in the early 17th century as enslaved Africans fled the sugar plantations of Pernambuco into the forested Serra da Barriga. By the 1670s it was a federation of villages with perhaps several thousand people, ruled from the fortified capital of Macaco by a king called Ganga Zumba.

In 1678 Ganga Zumba accepted a treaty: freedom for those born in Palmares in exchange for moving to Cucaú and returning new runaways. Zumbi, his nephew, refused to hand back fugitives, and Ganga Zumba was soon poisoned. For sixteen years Zumbi defeated expedition after expedition.

In 1694 the governor hired the bandeirante Domingos Jorge Velho, whose army with artillery broke the palisades of Macaco. Zumbi escaped but was betrayed and killed on 20 November 1695; his head was displayed in Recife. Brazil now marks 20 November as Black Consciousness Day.
story.zh:
17世纪初，被奴役的非洲人逃离伯南布哥的甘蔗种植园，躲进林木茂密的巴里加山，帕尔马雷斯由此壮大。到17世纪70年代，它已是由众多村落组成的联盟，人口或达数千，国王甘加·尊巴坐镇设防的首都马卡科。

1678年甘加·尊巴接受和约：生于帕尔马雷斯者获得自由，条件是迁往库考并交还新逃来的奴隶。他的侄子尊比拒绝交出逃亡者，甘加·尊巴不久被毒杀。此后十六年间，尊比一次次击退讨伐军。

1694年，总督雇用拓荒者多明戈斯·若热·韦柳，其军队以火炮攻破马卡科的木栅。尊比突围，但遭人出卖，于1695年11月20日被杀，首级被悬挂在累西腓示众。如今巴西将11月20日定为“黑人觉醒日”。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Zumbi
R. K. Kent, “Palmares: An African State in Brazil”, Journal of African History 6:2 (1965)
Flávio dos Santos Gomes, Palmares: escravidão e liberdade no Atlântico Sul (Contexto, 2005)

note: Zumbi’s early life is known from a single later account; the birth year 1655 is traditional.

name.zh: 阿莱雅丁尼奥（安东尼奥·弗朗西斯科·利斯博阿）

role.en: Sculptor and architect of the Brazilian baroque
role.zh: 巴西巴洛克雕塑家、建筑师

summary.en: Son of a Portuguese builder and an enslaved African woman in the gold town of Vila Rica, Aleijadinho (“the little cripple”) carved and designed churches across Minas Gerais. Despite a disease that crippled his hands, he carved the twelve soapstone prophets of Congonhas.
summary.zh: 生于产金重镇维拉里卡，父亲是葡萄牙建筑匠，母亲是被奴役的非洲妇女。阿莱雅丁尼奥（意为“小跛子”）在米纳斯吉拉斯各地雕刻和设计教堂。尽管疾病使他双手残废，他仍完成了孔戈尼亚斯的十二尊皂石先知像。

label.zh: 生于维拉里卡（欧鲁普雷图）

label.en: Designs the church of São Francisco de Assis, Ouro Preto
label.zh: 设计欧鲁普雷图圣方济各堂

label.en: Begins the Passion figures and prophets at Congonhas
label.zh: 开始雕刻孔戈尼亚斯的受难群像与先知像

sources.title: Britannica: Aleijadinho
Rodrigo José Ferreira Bretas, Traços biográficos relativos ao finado Antônio Francisco Lisboa (1858)
UNESCO World Heritage: Sanctuary of Bom Jesus do Congonhas

note: Birth year is given as 1730 or 1738; 1738 follows his death record, which gave his age as 76.

role.en: Kuraka and leader of the great Andean rebellion
role.zh: 原住民首领，安第斯大起义领袖

summary.en: José Gabriel Condorcanqui, a muleteer and Indigenous chief who claimed descent from the last Inca, launched the largest colonial uprising in Spanish America in November 1780 by hanging the corregidor Antonio de Arriaga. Captured in April 1781, he was executed in Cusco with his wife Micaela Bastidas.
summary.zh: 何塞·加夫列尔·孔多尔坎基是骡队商人兼原住民首领，自称末代印加后裔。1780年11月他绞死地方长官安东尼奥·德·阿里亚加，发动西属美洲规模最大的殖民地起义。1781年4月被俘，与妻子米凯拉·巴斯蒂达斯一同在库斯科被处决。

label.en: Seizes and hangs the corregidor Arriaga at Tinta
label.zh: 在廷塔逮捕并绞死长官阿里亚加

label.en: Defeats a Spanish column at Sangarará
label.zh: 在桑加拉拉击败西班牙军队
在兰圭附近遭出卖被俘
在库斯科中央广场被处决

story.en:
Condorcanqui had spent years petitioning colonial courts against the forced labour of the Potosí mita and the forced sale of goods by provincial officials. On 4 November 1780 he seized the corregidor of Tinta after a dinner, made him write letters summoning money and arms, and hanged him six days later before thousands of people.

Calling himself Túpac Amaru Inca, he defeated a Spanish force at Sangarará and gathered tens of thousands of followers, while his wife Micaela Bastidas ran supplies and correspondence. But he hesitated before Cusco, which he besieged only in January 1781, and royal troops from Lima drove him back.

Betrayed by his own officers, he was taken to Cusco. On 18 May 1781 he was forced to watch the execution of his wife and son, then four horses tried to tear him apart before he was beheaded. The rebellion continued under his relatives and the Aymara leader Túpac Katari, and an estimated 100,000 people died.
story.zh:
孔多尔坎基多年来一直向殖民法院申诉，反对波托西矿役制度和地方官员强制摊派商品。1780年11月4日，他在一次晚宴后扣押了廷塔的地方长官，迫其写信调集钱款和武器，六天后当着数千人将其绞死。

他自称图帕克·阿马鲁·印卡，在桑加拉拉击败西班牙军，聚集了数万追随者，妻子米凯拉·巴斯蒂达斯负责补给和通信。但他在库斯科城下犹豫不决，直到1781年1月才开始围城，被利马来的王军击退。

他被部下出卖，押往库斯科。1781年5月18日，他被迫目睹妻子和儿子被处决，随后四匹马试图将他五马分尸，最终被斩首。起义在他的亲属和艾马拉首领图帕克·卡塔里领导下继续，估计约十万人死亡。

sources.title: Britannica: Túpac Amaru II
Charles F. Walker, The Tupac Amaru Rebellion (Harvard UP, 2014)
Ward Stavig, The World of Túpac Amaru (University of Nebraska Press, 1999)

role.zh: 起义领袖、谋士

summary.en: Wife of Túpac Amaru II, Micaela Bastidas managed the rebellion’s supplies, recruitment and discipline and urged a swift attack on Cusco. Captured with her husband, she was executed in Cusco on 18 May 1781.
summary.zh: 图帕克·阿马鲁二世之妻，负责起义军的补给、招募和纪律，并力主迅速进攻库斯科。她与丈夫一同被俘，1781年5月18日在库斯科被处决。

label.en: Marries José Gabriel Condorcanqui at Surimana
label.zh: 在苏里马纳与何塞·加夫列尔·孔多尔坎基成婚

label.en: Directs the rebel headquarters at Tinta
label.zh: 在廷塔主持起义军大本营

sources.title: Wikipedia: Micaela Bastidas
Charles F. Walker, The Tupac Amaru Rebellion (Harvard UP, 2014)

note: Birthplace is given as Pampamarca or Tamburco in Apurímac.

role.zh: 南美北部的解放者

summary.en: A wealthy Caracas creole, Bolívar led the wars that freed Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia from Spain between 1813 and 1825. He presided over Gran Colombia, but his dream of a united Spanish America collapsed, and he died of tuberculosis on his way into exile.
summary.zh: 加拉加斯的富裕土生白人，1813至1825年间领导了使委内瑞拉、哥伦比亚、厄瓜多尔、秘鲁和玻利维亚摆脱西班牙统治的战争。他出任大哥伦比亚总统，但统一西属美洲的梦想破灭，在流亡途中死于肺结核。

label.en: Vows on the Monte Sacro in Rome to free his country
label.zh: 在罗马圣山立誓解放祖国

label.en: In exile, writes the Jamaica Letter at Kingston
label.zh: 流亡中在金斯敦写下《牙买加来信》
在安戈斯图拉国会发表演说

label.en: Climbs the Cerro Rico at Potosí
Dies at San Pedro Alejandrino, Santa Marta
label.zh: 卒于圣玛尔塔的圣佩德罗-亚历杭德里诺庄园

story.en:
Orphaned young and widowed within a year of marriage, Bolívar travelled in Europe and, according to his tutor Simón Rodríguez, swore on Rome’s Monte Sacro in 1805 to break Spain’s chains. Back in Venezuela he joined the patriots of 1810, saw the First Republic fall in 1812 and fled to Cartagena, where he blamed its collapse on weak federal government.

His “Admirable Campaign” retook Caracas in 1813, but royalist llaneros crushed the Second Republic. From exile in Jamaica he wrote a famous letter predicting the shape of independent Spanish America. Returning with Haitian help, he made the Orinoco his base and in 1819 led his army over the flooded llanos and the icy Páramo de Pisba to win at Boyacá.

Victories at Carabobo, Pichincha, Junín and Ayacucho followed, and Bolivia took his name. Yet Gran Colombia fractured, an assassination attempt in Bogotá in 1828 nearly killed him, and he died at 47, writing that those who serve a revolution “plough the sea”.
story.zh:
玻利瓦尔幼年父母双亡，婚后不到一年又丧妻，随后游历欧洲。据其老师西蒙·罗德里格斯记载，1805年他在罗马圣山立誓要打破西班牙的枷锁。回到委内瑞拉后，他加入1810年的爱国者行列，1812年目睹第一共和国覆灭，逃往卡塔赫纳，把失败归咎于软弱的联邦政府。

1813年他的“惊人战役”收复加拉加斯，但保王派平原骑兵摧毁了第二共和国。流亡牙买加期间，他写下著名的书信，预言独立后西属美洲的格局。在海地援助下他重返故土，以奥里诺科河流域为根据地，1819年率军穿越被洪水淹没的平原和冰冷的皮斯巴高原，在博亚卡获胜。

此后卡拉沃沃、皮钦查、胡宁和阿亚库乔连战告捷，玻利维亚以他的名字命名。然而大哥伦比亚分崩离析，1828年波哥大的一次刺杀几乎夺去他的性命。他47岁去世，留下“为革命效力的人犹如在海上耕耘”的感叹。

sources.title: Britannica: Simón Bolívar
John Lynch, Simón Bolívar: A Life (Yale UP, 2006)
Simón Bolívar, Carta de Jamaica (6 September 1815)

role.en: Liberator of Argentina, Chile and Peru
role.zh: 阿根廷、智利和秘鲁的解放者

summary.en: Born in the Jesuit mission town of Yapeyú and trained for 22 years in the Spanish army, San Martín returned in 1812 to serve Buenos Aires. He crossed the Andes in 1817, freed Chile at Chacabuco and Maipú, and proclaimed Peru’s independence in 1821, then withdrew after meeting Bolívar at Guayaquil.
summary.zh: 生于耶稣会传教镇亚佩尤，在西班牙军中服役22年，1812年回到布宜诺斯艾利斯效力。1817年他翻越安第斯山，在查卡布科和迈普解放智利，1821年宣布秘鲁独立，在瓜亚基尔会见玻利瓦尔后引退。

label.en: Wins his first battle at San Lorenzo
Leads the Army of the Andes out of Mendoza
label.zh: 率安第斯军从门多萨出发
在瓜亚基尔会见玻利瓦尔
在流亡地滨海布洛涅去世

story.en:
San Martín left the Río de la Plata as a child and grew up a Spanish officer, fighting the French at Bailén in 1808. In 1812 he resigned and sailed to Buenos Aires, convinced that the revolution could only be secured by striking at the royalist heart in Lima.

As governor of Cuyo he spent three years in Mendoza building the Army of the Andes, with foundries, uniforms sewn by local women and freed slaves in its ranks. In January 1817 about 5,000 men crossed the Andes in several columns, the main body through the Los Patos pass at over 4,000 metres, and surprised the royalists at Chacabuco.

After Maipú he sailed for Peru with Lord Cochrane’s fleet and entered Lima in 1821. At Guayaquil in July 1822 he met Bolívar privately; no record of their talk survives. He left the field to Bolívar, refused to take sides in Argentina’s civil wars, and lived his last decades in France.
story.zh:
圣马丁幼年离开拉普拉塔，在西班牙军中成长为军官，1808年在拜伦与法军作战。1812年他辞去军职航行至布宜诺斯艾利斯，认定只有打击利马的保王派心脏，革命才能稳固。

他出任库约省长，在门多萨用三年时间组建安第斯军：建铸造厂，由当地妇女缝制军装，并吸收获释奴隶入伍。1817年1月约五千人分几路翻越安第斯山，主力经海拔四千多米的洛斯帕托斯山口，在查卡布科出其不意地击败保王军。

迈普战役后，他随科克伦勋爵的舰队远征秘鲁，1821年进入利马。1822年7月他在瓜亚基尔与玻利瓦尔秘密会谈，谈话内容没有留下记录。他把战场让给玻利瓦尔，拒绝卷入阿根廷内战，晚年在法国度过。

sources.title: Britannica: José de San Martín
John Lynch, San Martín: Argentine Soldier, American Hero (Yale UP, 2009)
Bartolomé Mitre, Historia de San Martín y de la emancipación sudamericana (1887–1888)

name.zh: 安东尼奥·何塞·德·苏克雷

role.en: General; first constitutional president of Bolivia
role.zh: 将军，玻利维亚首任宪法总统

summary.en: Bolívar’s most trusted general won the battles of Pichincha (1822) and Ayacucho (1824), which ended Spanish rule in South America. He became Bolivia’s first president, resigned after a mutiny in 1828, and was assassinated in the mountains of Berruecos in 1830.
summary.zh: 玻利瓦尔最信任的将领，赢得皮钦查（1822年）和阿亚库乔（1824年）战役，终结了西班牙在南美的统治。他出任玻利维亚首任总统，1828年兵变后辞职，1830年在贝鲁埃科斯山中遇刺。

label.en: Wins the battle of Pichincha above Quito
label.zh: 在基多上方赢得皮钦查战役

label.en: Convenes the assembly that founds Bolivia at Chuquisaca
label.zh: 在丘基萨卡召集建立玻利维亚的议会

sources.title: Britannica: Antonio José de Sucre
John Lynch, The Spanish American Revolutions, 1808–1826 (2nd ed., Norton, 1986)

role.zh: 智利最高执政官

summary.en: The illegitimate son of the Irish-born viceroy Ambrosio O’Higgins, Bernardo led Chilean patriots in the independence war, crossed the Andes with San Martín and became Supreme Director after Chacabuco. He signed Chile’s declaration of independence in 1818 but was forced to abdicate in 1823.
summary.zh: 爱尔兰裔总督安布罗西奥·奥希金斯的私生子，在独立战争中领导智利爱国者，与圣马丁一同翻越安第斯山，查卡布科战役后出任最高执政官。他于1818年签署智利独立宣言，1823年被迫下台。

label.en: Defeated at Rancagua; flees to Mendoza
label.zh: 在兰卡瓜战败，逃往门多萨

sources.title: Britannica: Bernardo O’Higgins
Simon Collier & William F. Sater, A History of Chile, 1808–2002 (Cambridge UP, 2004)

role.zh: 革命者、玻利瓦尔的伴侣

summary.en: A Quito creole who left her English husband for Simón Bolívar, Manuela Sáenz served as his archivist and confidante and was made a colonel. In September 1828 she helped him escape assassins in Bogotá, earning the title “Liberator of the Liberator”. She died in poverty at Paita.
summary.zh: 基多的土生白人女子，离开英国丈夫追随西蒙·玻利瓦尔，担任他的档案管理人和心腹，并获上校军衔。1828年9月她在波哥大帮助玻利瓦尔躲过刺客，被誉为“解放者的解放者”。她在派塔贫病而终。

label.en: Meets Bolívar at his triumphal entry into Quito
label.zh: 在玻利瓦尔凯旋进入基多时与他相识

label.en: Serves with the army in the Ayacucho campaign
label.zh: 随军参加阿亚库乔战役

label.en: Saves Bolívar from assassins in Bogotá
label.zh: 在波哥大从刺客手中救出玻利瓦尔

label.en: Dies in a diphtheria epidemic at Paita

sources.title: Britannica: Manuela Sáenz
Pamela S. Murray, For Glory and Bolívar: The Remarkable Life of Manuela Sáenz (University of Texas Press, 2008)

role.en: First emperor of Brazil, King Pedro IV of Portugal
role.zh: 巴西首任皇帝，葡萄牙国王佩德罗四世

summary.en: Son of John VI, Pedro came to Rio with the fleeing court in 1808 and stayed as regent when his father returned to Lisbon. He declared Brazil’s independence in 1822 and was crowned emperor, abdicated in 1831 in favour of his five-year-old son and died after winning Portugal’s civil war for his daughter.
summary.zh: 若昂六世之子，1808年随出逃的王室来到里约，父亲返回里斯本后留任摄政。1822年宣布巴西独立并加冕为皇帝，1831年退位给五岁的儿子，为女儿赢得葡萄牙内战后去世。

label.en: Arrives in Rio with the royal court
Cry of Ipiranga at São Paulo
label.zh: 在圣保罗发出“伊皮兰加呐喊”

label.en: Holds Porto in the Liberal Wars
label.zh: 在自由战争中坚守波尔图

sources.title: Britannica: Pedro I
Neill Macaulay, Dom Pedro: The Struggle for Liberty in Brazil and Portugal, 1798–1834 (Duke UP, 1986)

role.zh: 巴西皇帝

summary.en: Emperor from the age of five and ruling in person from 1840, Pedro II gave Brazil half a century of stable constitutional government. A scholar who corresponded with Darwin, Pasteur and Victor Hugo, he led Brazil through the Paraguayan War and towards abolition, and was deposed by the army in 1889.
summary.zh: 五岁即位，1840年起亲政，为巴西带来半个世纪稳定的立宪统治。他是一位学者，与达尔文、巴斯德、雨果等通信，带领巴西经历巴拉圭战争并走向废奴，1889年被军队废黜。

label.en: Born at the São Cristóvão palace, Rio
label.zh: 生于里约圣克里斯托旺宫

label.en: Witnesses the Paraguayan surrender at Uruguaiana
label.zh: 在乌拉圭亚纳目睹巴拉圭军投降

label.en: Tries Bell’s telephone at the Philadelphia Centennial
label.zh: 在费城百年博览会上试用贝尔电话

story.en:
When Pedro I abdicated in April 1831, he left behind a five-year-old son as emperor. Regents governed through a decade of provincial revolts until, in 1840, parliament declared the 14-year-old of age. The boy who had grown up among tutors and books became a conscientious, austere monarch.

He spoke many languages, studied Hebrew and Sanskrit, founded schools and observatories and travelled widely. At the 1876 Centennial Exhibition in Philadelphia he picked up Alexander Graham Bell’s telephone and is said to have exclaimed that it talked. He used his moderating power to rotate Liberal and Conservative cabinets.

The long Paraguayan War raised the army’s political ambitions, and abolition in 1888 alienated planters. On 15 November 1889 officers proclaimed a republic. Pedro II accepted exile without resistance and died in a Paris hotel two years later; his remains returned to Brazil in 1921.
story.zh:
1831年4月佩德罗一世退位，留下五岁的儿子继位。摄政们在十年间应对各省叛乱，直到1840年议会宣布14岁的皇帝成年。这个在家庭教师和书本中长大的少年，成为一位勤勉而简朴的君主。

他通晓多种语言，研习希伯来文和梵文，兴办学校和天文台，四处游历。在1876年费城百年博览会上，他拿起亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔的电话，据说惊呼“它会说话”。他运用宪法赋予的“调节权”轮换自由党与保守党内阁。

旷日持久的巴拉圭战争助长了军队的政治野心，1888年废奴又使种植园主离心。1889年11月15日军官们宣布成立共和国。佩德罗二世不作抵抗接受流放，两年后在巴黎一家旅馆去世；1921年他的遗骸被迎回巴西。

summary.zh: 佩德罗二世的长女，在父亲出国期间三度担任摄政。她于1871年签署《自由出生法》，1888年5月13日签署彻底废除奴隶制的《黄金法》；十八个月后帝制覆灭，她在法国度过余生。

summary.en: A gaúcho politician who seized power in the Revolution of 1930, Vargas ruled Brazil until 1945, from 1937 as dictator of the Estado Novo. He built a labour code, state steel and oil industries and a populist following, returned as elected president in 1951 and shot himself in 1954 amid a political crisis.

summary.en: A poor provincial girl who became a radio actress in Buenos Aires, Eva Duarte married Juan Perón in 1945 and became the passionate voice of Peronism. Through her foundation she ran hospitals and schools, and she led the campaign for women’s suffrage in 1947 before dying of cancer at 33.
summary.zh: 出身外省贫寒家庭，在布宜诺斯艾利斯成为广播剧演员。伊娃·杜阿尔特1945年嫁给胡安·庇隆，成为庇隆主义充满激情的代言人。她通过自己的基金会兴办医院和学校，1947年领导争取妇女选举权的运动，33岁死于癌症。

story.en:
Eva Duarte was the youngest of five children born to an unmarried mother in the pampas town of Los Toldos. At fifteen she went to Buenos Aires and worked her way up from small theatre parts to starring roles in radio dramas. In January 1944 she met Colonel Perón at a benefit for victims of the San Juan earthquake.

They married in October 1945, days after workers’ demonstrations freed him from arrest. As first lady she received petitioners for hours each day, and her Eva Perón Foundation distributed sewing machines, built hospitals, schools and children’s homes, and organised the women’s branch of the Peronist party. Women voted nationally for the first time in 1951.

Already ill with cervical cancer, she declined the vice-presidential nomination before a vast crowd in August 1951. She died on 26 July 1952; her embalmed body was later stolen by the military, hidden in Italy for 16 years and only returned to Argentina in 1974.
story.zh:
伊娃·杜阿尔特生于潘帕斯草原小镇洛斯托尔多斯，是一位未婚母亲所生五个孩子中最小的一个。15岁时她来到布宜诺斯艾利斯，从小剧场的配角一路做到广播剧主角。1944年1月，她在为圣胡安地震灾民举办的义演上结识了庇隆上校。

1945年10月工人示威使庇隆获释，几天后两人结婚。作为第一夫人，她每天花数小时接见请愿者；她的伊娃·庇隆基金会分发缝纫机，兴建医院、学校和儿童之家，并组建了庇隆党的妇女分部。1951年阿根廷妇女首次在全国选举中投票。

1951年8月，已身患宫颈癌的她在广场的人海面前放弃副总统提名。她于1952年7月26日去世；遗体经防腐处理后被军方盗走，秘藏意大利16年，直到1974年才回到阿根廷。

role.zh: 智利总统

summary.en: A physician and founder of Chile’s Socialist Party, Allende ran for president four times and won in 1970 as candidate of the Popular Unity coalition, the first Marxist elected to lead a Latin American democracy. He nationalised copper and banks; he died during the military coup of 11 September 1973.
summary.zh: 医生出身，智利社会党创始人之一，四次竞选总统，1970年作为人民团结联盟候选人当选，是拉丁美洲第一位通过民主选举执政的马克思主义者。他将铜矿和银行收归国有，1973年9月11日军事政变中身亡。

summary.en: Lucila Godoy Alcayaga, a rural schoolteacher from the Elqui valley, became the first Latin American writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1945). She helped reform Mexican schools, served as Chilean consul across Europe and the Americas, and wrote of children, motherhood and the Andean landscape.

One Hundred Years of Solitude (1967) made him the leading voice of magical realism and the Latin American Boom; he won the Nobel Prize in 1982.

summary.en: Niemeyer brought sensuous curves to modernist concrete, first at the Pampulha complex in Belo Horizonte and then in the palaces, cathedral and ministries of Brasília. A lifelong communist, he worked in exile in France after the 1964 coup and kept designing until his death at 104.
